hypotheses.title: Calibrated Volume Gate Liquidity Absorption Reversion (volume > 1.2 * adv20)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Batch 220 Candidate 3 achieved Sharpe 1.77, Sub-universe Sharpe 1.47, Turnover 40.03%, and Fitness 0.91 at Decay 2 with zero portfolio correlation. By tightening the entry threshold from volume > adv20 to volume > 1.2 * adv20, we restrict trades strictly to acute institutional liquidity dislocations where mean-reversion is strongest, while trade_when(..., -1) preserves positions during normal volume sessions. This reduces annual turnover by ~25-30% (from 40% down to ~28-30%) without sacrificing return, mathematically lifting Fitness from 0.91 past the 1.00 qualification threshold to ~1.08+.
confounders: Persistent multi-day momentum runs triggered by large earnings or M&A surprises that exceed 1.2x ADV
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if tightening the volume filter from 1.0 to 1.2 excessively reduces sample size or drops Sharpe below 1.50.

hypotheses.title: Volatility-Normalized Liquidity Absorption with 1.15x Volume Filter
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Batch 220 Candidate 2 achieved Sharpe 1.75, Sub-universe Sharpe 1.60, and Turnover 38.47% with Fitness 0.86. Dividing 3-day close price delta by trailing 10-day rolling standard deviation (ts_delta(close, 3) / ts_std_dev(close, 10)) scales the price excursion into a dimensionless volatility metric. Raising the trade trigger to volume > 1.15 * adv20 dampens marginal trade executions, reducing turnover below 30% and enabling Fitness to cross the 1.00 cutoff.
confounders: Sustained volatility expansion regimes where price standard deviation inflates faster than price moves
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if 1.15x volume filter fails to drop turnover or deteriorates Sub-universe Sharpe below 1.00.

hypotheses.title: Uniformly Ranked Dollar Volume Absorption with 1.2x Volume Gate
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Combining uniform cross-sectional ranking (group_rank) with the tightened 1.2x ADV filter eliminates tail risk while capturing the full alpha from order book absorption. When trading volume exceeds 20% above its 20-day baseline, temporary liquidity imbalances create predictable 3-day price mean-reversions across the TOP3000 universe. Holding positions during non-shock periods (-1) maintains optimal capital allocation while keeping turnover below 30%.
confounders: Broad market liquidity droughts where volume remains below 1.2x ADV for extended periods
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if group_rank underperforms group_zscore due to equal allocation across varying dislocation severities.
